title: Anchor loadbook and checkpoint replay procedure
content:
Purpose
This doc describes a practical procedure for creating an anchor-based loadbook and using reproducible checkpoint snapshots to replay traffic during throughput benchmarking. The goal is to produce repeatable, defensible throughput numbers while preserving fidelity to production-like arrival patterns and cache/kv-state priming. This is intended to sit alongside our other loadgen playbooks; it focuses on a checkpoint-and-replay model to reduce variance across long-run experiments.

Scope
- Target: serving-runtime teams running GPU-backed model endpoints.
- Workloads: text generation / chat-style tokens, variable sequence lengths, multi-model fanout.
- Not covered in detail: latency microprofiling (still use perf traces), model-level accuracy regressions (use eval harness).

High-level idea
1) Curate a set of traffic "anchors" (representative request batch) that reflect the real distribution we care about (seq length, prompt types, temperature).
2) Prime the runtime with a checkpoint capture that includes KV cache state (where applicable), model variant, and client-side RNG seeds.
3) Use the loadbook to drive a deterministic replay engine which issues requests against the runtime under controlled pacing patterns (fixed, poisson, micro-burst).
4) Collect telemetry across long windows, compare stability anchors between runs, and apply a checkpoint re-priming step between experiments to reset state.

Why checkpoints?
- Reduces cold-start noise from model loading and kernel JIT orthogonal to throughput numbers.
- Ensures the same internal cache occupancy and KV layout across runs, improving repeatability.
- Enables faster iteration: restore snapshot -> run -> compare.

Definitions
- Anchor: a single JSON request template (prompt + settings) chosen to represent a class of production load.
- Loadbook: ordered list of anchors + meta (weights, timestamps distribution, client ids).
- Checkpoint snapshot: persisted runtime state (model weights already resident, KV caches for warm context, selected quantization path state) captured from a live instance.

Anchor selection and curation
- Select 8–16 anchors per workload vertical (short prompts, medium chat, long-context summarization).
- For each anchor capture: prompt text, max_tokens, stop tokens, temperature, top_k/top_p, example seed, and an estimate of output token length distribution.
- Tag anchors with: occupancy_bucket (short/med/long), expected KV hits ratio, and a unique stable id.
- Validate anchors by running 50 short warm runs and measuring token distribution and average response length; discard outliers.

Checkpoint capture procedure
1) Provision an isolated runtime node (dedicated test slice) with the target model and exact config.
2) Ensure model weights are loaded and JIT kernels warmed (see kernel-warm-run checklist below).
3) Issue a scripted priming sequence made from the chosen anchors (weighting applied) for 10–15 minutes or until KV cache hit-rate stabilizes and GPU mem clock/temperature are in steady range. Record priming log.
4) Trigger snapshot capture: persist necessary runtime internals (KV slots, key->value mapping summary, RNG seeds used for the priming run, model version tag, binary ident, and runtime config). Note: due to privacy/legal concerns we persist only internal cache metadata, not customer payloads.
5) Store the snapshot with a SHA256 and metadata file (anchor-set, priming-duration, node-id, gpu-serial).

Kernel warm-run checklist (before snapshot)
- Run a short sequence of varied-length requests (with representative anchors) for 2× average request length to ensure jit/kernels compiled.
- Verify NVML reports stable clocks and no background eviction events.
- Confirm that observed kernel launch latencies have stabilized (see perf_counter kernels/launch_ms).

Replay harness: deterministic replay with pacing
- Replay engine must accept: snapshot-id, loadbook id, pacing profile, rng-seed-overrides, client-count.
- Pacing profiles supported: fixed-interval, poisson(lambda), bursty-leaky-bucket (burst_size, drain_rate), and paced-concurrency (target concurrent in-flight requests).
- For repeatability prefer fixed-interval or seeded poisson with explicit timestamp seeds.
- Replay engine rehydrates the checkpoint on the target node before sending traffic. Ensure exclusive node use to avoid cross-tenant noise.

Seed management and RNG hygiene
- All client-side seeds used to generate sampling randomness must be recorded in the snapshot metadata.
- When replaying, provide the recorded seeds or a deterministic replay mapping function.
- Avoid system clocks as a seed source; instead use recorded epoch seeds.

Metric capture and aggregation windows
- Collect continuous metrics at 1s granularity: qps, tokens/s, p50/p90/p99 latency, GPU util, GPU memory, CUDA kernel times, host CPU, net drop/retransmit, rpc retries.
- Use a warm-up discard window of first N minutes (N = max(5, priming_minutes/2)). Only compute final throughput on the steady-state window defined by: after warm discard and when 5-min sliding stddev of tokens/s < 3%.
- Report both raw sliding-window peak and a stability-anchored mean (mean over N contiguous stable minutes).

Stability anchors and regression comparisons
- Each lab run includes a small set of canonical anchors (2–4) that act as stability probes. Track their p90 latency and tokens/s over all experiments to detect drift.
- If stability anchors deviate >5% from prior baseline for the same snapshot and hardware, mark run as suspect and investigate thermal/P-state changes, background processes, or driver updates.

Noise sources and mitigation
- Thermal throttling: monitor GPU temperature and power limits. Use node preconditioning (30 min burn-in) when benchmarking long runs.
- Background kernel scheduling: isolate test nodes and stop cron/system jobs. Use cgroup pinning for loadgen process.
- Network jitter: run replay on the same rack/VLAN; avoid cross-region tests for stability baselines.
- Model version drift: lock to exact model artifact id and runtime binary.

Run orchestration pattern (recommended)
1) Restore snapshot to node A. Run smoke replay for 2 minutes to validate snapshot health.
2) Execute full warm priming sequence for checkpoint revalidation if needed (short 3–5 minute priming).
3) Start main replay with configured pacing for target duration (recommended 60–180 minutes depending on SLO).
4) After run, collect artifacts: telemetry dump, kernel traces (if enabled), loadgen logs, and snapshot usage metrics.
5) Run post-analysis script comparing stability anchors and producing summary table.

Example loadgen config snippet (pseudo)
- snapshot_id: s-20251112-01
- anchors: [A03, A07, A12]
- anchor_weights: [0.5, 0.3, 0.2]
- pacing: poisson_lambda: 40, seed: 12345
- clients: 12
- concurrency_limit: 48
- duration_minutes: 120
- discard_warm_minutes: 10

Expected outputs and artifacts
- throughput-summary.csv (minute-level tokens/s, qps, latencies)
- priming-log.txt (anchor priming events)
- snapshot-metadata.json (human readable metadata stored with snapshot SHA)
- kernel-launch-trace.out (if tracing enabled)
- run-evidence.tar.gz (all logs + telemetry + git tag of loadgen used)

Post-run forensic checklist
- confirm snapshot id matches expected hash
- validate window selection (was discard window applied?)
- compare canonical anchor metrics to baseline
- inspect GPU power/clock history for anomalies

Common pitfalls observed (lab notes)
- Restoring a snapshot after a driver update can silently change kernel selection and produce subtle throughput shifts; always pair snapshots with runtime binary ids.
- Over-aggressive caching of request payloads in the loadgen can hide serialization overhead—ensure payloads are materialized per request during final runs.
- Ignoring small variance early in a long run leads to incorrect peaks; always use sliding-window stability criteria.

Ownership and cadence
- Primary owner: Maya Chen (eng-serving-runtime).
- Secondary: Rajiv Patel (perf infra), Evelyn Ortiz (observability).
- Keep anchor-set review cadence to 6 weeks or after any major model change.

Next steps / TODOs
- Add an automated snapshot validation step in the loadbench CI that verifies snapshot rehydrates cleanly on staged hardware. (see linked PR)
- Experiment: compare checkpoint restore + replay vs full cold-start runs for 1h plateau stability on A100 and H100.
- Create small internal dashboard that surfaces canonical anchor drift over time.

Appendix: experiment log template (one-line per run)
- run_id | snapshot_id | node | model_tag | pacing | clients | start | duration | steady_mean_tokens_per_s | p90_anchor_diff_pct | notes

- Kernel trace best-practices: confluence.redwood/serving/kernel-traces (internal)
